properties.name: Coricancha & Lake Puray
properties.subtitle: Cusco Region, Peru
properties.claim: The Temple of the Sun, whose walls were sheathed in gold and whose garden held life-sized gold maize and llamas, is presented as the repository of off-world metalworking — and the forty-one ceque sightlines radiating from it as a surveyed grid.
properties.context: Coricancha's Inca walls survive beneath the Dominican convent built over them, and the gold's fate is documented: it was stripped for Atahualpa's ransom and melted, recorded in Spanish accounts with weights. The ceque system was reconstructed by Bernabé Cobo and analysed by Tom Zuidema and Brian Bauer — a genuine radial organisation of shrines, calendar and kin groups, and a major achievement of Andean spatial thought.
properties.summary: The Coricancha (Cusco Quechua: Quri Kancha, lit. 'golden temple', pronounced [ˈqɔɾi ˈkantʃa]) was the most important temple in the Inca Empire, and was described by early Spanish colonialists. It is located in Cusco, Peru, which was the capital of the empire.
